<thought>The 13C NMR shows a low-field peak at 14.26 ppm, which is typical for a simple alkyl methyl carbon. There is also a peak at 61.10 ppm, which falls in the region for a carbon attached to an electronegative atom (e.g., a methoxy –OCH₃ group). Both correspond to CH₃ groups. Therefore, the molecule contains two distinct methyl groups.</thought>
<final_answer>2</final_answer>
